references.text: Isaiah also mentions wheat and spelt as important grain crops in Israel, describing how the farmer sows them correctly.
Ezekiel mentions wheat and spelt among the grains used to make bread in Israel.
The preceding verse explains that the flax and barley were struck down, providing context for why the wheat and spelt were spared—they matured later.
Wheat is mentioned as one of the important crops in the Promised Land, underscoring its significance in Israelite agriculture.
Both verses illustrate God's provision and protection of food sources during famine.
A clear theological contrast: Hosea shows the hunger of judgment, while Exodus shows God's protection of the harvest.
